 1m ago 10.29 EST A double change for Liverpool, who bring Szoboszlai and Barcola off and Munoz and Nyoni on.
 Share 5m ago 10.26 EST Palace are trying, a bit clumsily at present, to find a way back into this game. Osorio tries to find a way past Kerkez, but the Liverpool defender throws himself to the ground and wins a free kick.
 Share 10m ago 10.20 EST Yellow card! The specific thing Barcola was threatening there was Pino’s ankle, and into the book he goes.
 Share 11m ago 10.19 EST Another chance for Liverpool, but Mitchell slides in to block a cross-shot from Barcola, who has switched to the right flank at half-time and looks much more threatening for it.
 Share 13m ago 10.18 EST A point of information from Grant Kempton, regarding the Igor Thiago red card: “Just to correct. Chema was booked ... taken off at half time because of the booking. But its still force into the face so booking and red card sounds right.” Ah fair dos.
 Share 15m ago 10.16 EST GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-2 Liverpool (Wirtz, 54 mins)
 Liverpool double their lead! Barcola is played down the right and sends in a nice low cross, possibly aiming for Isak, but it runs to Wirtz and he strokes it into the corner!
 View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz of Liverpool scores his team’s second goal. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.27 EST 20m ago 10.10 EST Two players run clear for Crystal Palace, and Wharton just has to slide the ball across for Strand Larsen to turn it in! But his pass is abysmal, Strand Larsen can’t reach it, and he’ll be grateful in the circumstances that he was about 10 yards offside when the ball was played through.
 Share 22m ago 10.08 EST “Re the Thiago sending-off, we saw last week with the shirt-pull on Isak that wasn’t punished precisely why players over-exaggerate,” writes Andy Flintoff. For sure, but if someone hits your chin and you go down holding your forehead, you’re not drawing the referee’s attention to a foul, you’re cheating.
 Share 24m ago 10.07 EST GOAL! Ipswich 0-2 Bournemouth (Davis own goal, 46 mins)
 The second half has started with a bang at Ipswich! An own-bang! Christie shoots from the left of goal, with his left foot and not from a great position, but you don’t win the lottery unless you buy a ticket, and the ball comes off Leif Davis and flies into the net!
 Share 35m ago 09.56 EST “I haven’t seen the hands to the face, I’m busy cooking and with no TV in the kitchen I can’t watch but am just following here,” writes George Ronczy. “If Andres was hit in the neck and grabbed his forehead, he should get booked for simulation.” Absolute and complete agreement from me: the officials may decide that Igor Thiago’s push was violent enough to deserve a red card, it seemed harsh to me but an argument can be made for it. However Andres certainly overdramatised the situation and there should be repercussions for that also.
 Also, what’s on the menu?

 We have now had half of the time and the Premier scores are as follows:
 Brighton 2-0 Brentford
 Crystal Palace 0-1 Liverpool
 Ipswich 0-1 Bournemouth
 Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea

 Share 41m ago 09.50 EST In the third of three minutes’ stoppage time at Palace a Szoboszlai corner is flicked on to Araujo, five yards out, but he can’t react in time to do anything with it and the ball ends up in Henderson’s hands.
 Share 42m ago 09.49 EST GOAL! Brighton 2-0 Brentford (Gross penalty, 42 mins)
 An absolutely unstoppable penalty from Pascal Gross to double Brighton’s lead. Kelleher goes he right way, but that ball is top-corner-bound and there’s nothing he can do about it.
 Share 44m ago 09.47 EST I’ve now seen the penalty incident at the Stadium of Light, and it looks to me like the main reason Brobbey went down was that his right foot caught his left ankle, and he thus tripped himself up. He was, though, being bothered by Colwill, who made no attempt to play the ball and may well have made contact with that right leg before the self-trippage.
 Share 48m ago 09.43 EST The Palace game is pure chaos. About 80 seconds after his goal Mac Allister is flinging himself around the Liverpool penalty area to block Timber’s shot.
 Share 49m ago 09.42 EST GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-1 Liverpool (Mac Allister, 40 mins)
 Szoboszlai whips in the ball from a right-wing free-kick, and Mac Allister escapes his marker, meets it at the near post, and sends a low header beyond Henderson!
 View image in fullscreen Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister scores their first goal past Crystal Palace's Dean Henderson. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters Share Updated at  09.58 EST 50m ago 09.41 EST GOAL! Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea (Le Fee penalty, 36 mins)
 I haven’t seen the infringement that led to the penalty, but I have seen Le Fee send the keeper the wrong way from the spot!
 View image in fullscreen Enzo Le Fee of Sunderland scores a penalty. Photograph: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.17 EST 51m ago 09.40 EST Saved! Mitchell’s deep cross falls to Kamada, and unlike Barcola he manages to control his volley. But the shot flies too close to Alisson, who pushes it away!
 Share 52m ago 09.38 EST What a miss! Szoboszlai’s cross finds Barcola beyond the far post, completely unmarked and able to watch the ball dip towards his instep and pick his spot! Unfortunately the spot he picks is approximately 40 rows back in the stand.
 Share 54m ago 09.36 EST The ball came off a Palace player, and offside it is. An escape for Liverpool, who were controlling this game for a while but are certainly not dominating it currently.
 Share 1h ago 09.35 EST Goal disallowed! Some penalty-area ping-pong ends with the ball at Strand Larsen’s feet, five yards out, and he turns it in! But he’s given offside! VAR will have a look at this, of course, and the question is who the ball came off …
 Share 1h ago 09.34 EST Strand Larsen is found in space, but by the time he’s shooting distance from goal Van Dijk has come across, and he gets in the way of the shot.
 Share 1h ago 09.31 EST RED CARD! Brentford go down to 10 men!
 Brentford’s Igor Thiago is sent off for “pushing an opponent in the face with force”. Chema Andres had been hassling him for about 20 seconds of constant mini-fouling, and eventually Thiago has had enough of it and gives him a push. His hand catches his opponent’s chin, he goes down clutching his forehead, and VAR does the rest. It wasn’t nothing, for sure, but neither was it what Chema Andres pretended it was.
 View image in fullscreen Igor Thiago of Brentford pushes Chema Andres of Brighton and Hove Albion in the face which results in a red card. Photograph: Anthony Hanc/Wired Photos/Shutterstock Share Updated at  09.36 EST 1h ago 09.28 EST Another poor final pass from Liverpool, which allows Disasi to get there before Gakpo, and shepherd the ball out of play.
 Share 1h ago 09.27 EST It’s much more open now at Selhurst Park. Araujo goes into the book for a foul, and then a Liverpool counter is curtailed by a poor pass and a good interception from Wharton.
 Share 1h ago 09.27 EST “Liverpool fan here, but still, surely a push is a push?” writes Ric Latham of that push on Barcola. “It wasn’t shoulder to shoulder, the defender wasn’t challenging for the ball, all he was doing was (successfully) preventing Barcola from getting his head anywhere near it. It’s a stone cold pen in either box, and saying otherwise just normalises the idea that players should get away with things like this because it wasn’t clear enough. Maddening.” In the time it takes to read this email Tony Harrington, the referee, gives two soft free-kicks for pushing or blocking and it’s the inconsistency that’s really maddening. There were two hands on his back, but I didn’t see the defender’s arms straighten as they would if there was a real shove going on.
 Share 1h ago 09.21 EST GOAL! Brighton 1-0 Brentford (Diego Gomez, 15 mins)
 Brighton move to second in the league! A cross from the right is kind of cleared, from which another cross from the right is kind of cleared, at which point Diego Gomez seizes possession, decides he’s had enough of crosses, and bangs a left-footer into the top corner from 25 yards!
 View image in fullscreen Brighton and Hove Albion's Diego Gomez celebrates scoring their first goal with Chema Andres and Pascal Gross. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  09.23 EST 1h ago 09.19 EST They have now! A lovely switch of play gives the ball to Mitchell, who passes inside to Pino, who hammers a shot into the Liverpool crossbar!
 Share 1h ago 09.17 EST Szoboszlai now crosses from the left, Gakpo, beyond the far post, cushions it back across goal and it runs across the goalline without anyone there to turn it in! Palace haven’t been out of their half for a while.
 Share 1h ago 09.16 EST Save! Szoboszlai sends in a low, bobbling shot from 23 yards or thereabouts, which Henderson turns round the post.
 Share 1h ago 09.12 EST At Selhurst Park Barcola tries to meet a cross from the right and gets a fairly gentle push in the back as he does so. He goes down, but a penalty for that would be a bit much.
 Share 1h ago 09.09 EST GOAL! Ipswich 0-1 Bournemouth (Evanilson, 5 mins)
 A disastrous goal for Ipswich! Chris Walton, the home side’s keeper, tries to take the ball past the onrushing Evanilson, fails, is dispossessed, and the rest is a formality!
 View image in fullscreen Evanilson of Bournemouth scores against Ipswich Town at Portman Road. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.30 EST 1h ago 09.07 EST A glimpse of goal for Palace, as Mitchell’s driven cross is met by Strand Larsen, but he can’t do much more than get a foot to it, and he deflects it limply wide of goal, from where it’s cleared for a throw-in.
 Share 1h ago 09.05 EST I’m focusing, for now, on Crystal Palace v Liverpool, where Isak has just had half a chance, but rather than racing onto the ball he rather meandered up to it, and his shot then hit a defender.
 Share 1h ago 09.01 EST 2.01pm: Football o’clock!
 Share 2h ago 08.58 EST The players are out and action is imminent. There’ll be a minute’s silence before all the games, because it is Remembrance Sunday.
 Share 2h ago 08.37 EST Weather update! It’s sunny in Brighton …
 View image in fullscreen A view of the AmEx Stadium before Brighton’s game against Brentford in the Premier League. Photograph: Chris Roll/Action Plus/Shutterstock … cloudy in Ipswich …
 View image in fullscreen A view of Portman Road before Ipswich’s game against Bournemouth. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters … and it’s been raining in Sunderland.
 View image in fullscreen Sunderland fans arriving for the Premier League match against Chelsea at the Stadium of Light. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA Share 2h ago 08.30 EST Fabian Hurzeler on what makes Brighton good: “Brilliant at the basics. That’s our foundation. That’s what made us strong and hopefully will make us strong in the future. It’s not about first outplaying the opponent, it’s about outworking the opponent.”
 Share 2h ago 08.30 EST Marco Rose is asked to identify Ipswich’s threat to Bournemouth today, and his response is, I have to say, vicious: “They want to win the game, I’m quite sure. It’s a nice ground.”
 Share 2h ago 08.30 EST Team news!
 Team news has leaked (well, been published), and here are the lineups for the 2pm Premier League games:
 Brighton v Brentford
Brighton: Verbruggen, Costinha, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli, Gross, Andres, Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper, Kostoulas. Subs: Steele, Hadjam, Hinshelwood, Rutter, Minteh, Kadioglu, Wieffer, Svoboda, Yalcouye.
 Brentford: Kelleher, Kayode, Ajer, van den Berg, Hickey, Sangare, Janelt, Ouattara, Schade, Lewis-Potter, Thiago. Subs: Valdimarsson, Yarmolyuk, Jensen, Wilson, Anthony, Collins, Damsgaard, Diouf, Schuster.
 Referee: Michael Oliver.
 Crystal Palace v Liverpool
Crystal Palace: Henderson, Lerma, Richards, Disasi, Mingueza, Wharton, Timber, Mitchell, Kamada, Pino, Larsen. Subs: Benitez, Canvot, Nketiah, McNeil, Hughes, Osorio, Khalaili, Doucoure, Chilwell.
 Liverpool: Alisson, Araujo, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Gakpo, Wirtz, Barcola, Isak. Subs: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Tsimikas, Munoz, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.
 Referee: Tony Harrington (Cleveland).
 Ipswich v Bournemouth
Ipswich: Walton, Ouattara, O’Shea, Diop, Davis, Florentino, Palacios, Maeda, Enciso, Philogene-Bidace, Emersonn. Subs: Scherpen, Furlong, Matusiwa, Fatawu, Flemming, Lukic, Greaves, Akpom, Clarke.
 Bournemouth: Petrovic, Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert, Adams, Christie, Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier, Evanilson. Subs: Di Gregorio, Cook, Soler, Scott, Doak, Diakite, Adli, Junior Kroupi, Rodriguez.
 Referee: Simon Hooper.
 Sunderland v Chelsea
Sunderland: Roefs, Hume, Mukiele, O’Nien, Mandava, Xhaka, Sadiki, Meunier, Talbi, Le Fee, Brobbey. Subs: Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Nilson Angulo, Rigg, Isidor, Ahoka, Fofana, Tutierov.
 Chelsea: Penders, Palestra, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria, Caicedo, Lavia, Palmer, Henderson, Rogers, Pedro Neto. Subs: Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Welbeck, Emegha, Quenda, Gusto, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao.
 Referee: Jarred Gillett.
 Share 2h ago 08.30 EST Preamble
 Hello world! We have four intriguing Premier League matches ahead of us today, with the teams currently fourth (Chelsea) and sixth (Liverpool) in the table playing away to the teams in 20th (Sunderland) and 19th (Crystal Palace), while the early afternoon’s big clash, between Brighton and Brentford, gives us the prospect of Brighton – with more than a quarter of the season played mind you – moving to second in the table. Plus, bubbling away in the background, half a game in the Scottish Premiership, the best part of three in the WSL and a side-order of FA Cup action. So, and to summarise, welcome! Here are the 2pm Premier League fixtures:
 Brighton v Brentford
 Crystal Palace v Liverpool
 Ipswich Town v Bournemouth
 Sunderland v Chelsea
 And then at 4.30pm:
 Manchester United v Aston Villa
